course_name_original: Laboratory of chemistry applied to materials, energy and environment
course_name_en: Laboratory of chemistry applied to materials, energy and environment
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Chemistry and Physics: structural and chemical properties of matter, chemical equilibria (acid-base, redox), electromagnetic radiation-matter interactions.
Basic knowledge of statistics and experimental data management.
Chemistry and basi organic chemistry (140110) course

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the basic knowledge on the different analytical methods.
Be able to appropriately apply the analytical tools for identifying unknown compounds and quantifying mixture components.
Be able to consider the errors associated to the measurements.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: analytical techniques and sustainable chemical processes
Sampling, basic principles in laboratory, health and safety in the laboratory, instrumental calibration
Atomic spectroscopy: atomic absorption and emission.
Reference: experimental data management and statistics
Line 1: chemical analysis on materials (polymers, textiles fibers, paper, wood, concrete, ....)
Line 2: chemical analysis for energy (photovoltaic cells, batteries, ...)
Line 3: chemical analysis for environment (pollutants photocatalytic methods, materials degradation, emissions, ...)
Line 4: chemical analysi for food industry (oil and beverages, adulteration and sophistication, ...)

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation based on experimental methods and critical evaluation of experimental results from laboratory exercises
Written report based on the DOE study-case with statistical analysis and result discussion

assessment_rules: The final mark is a thirtieth grade, given by the weighted average of the result of the written group report (with weight 50%) and the score assigned for the oral presentation (weighting 50%).
bibliography: Notes, video recordings, exercises and PowerPoint slides provided by the teachers
